lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My composter's full. Know what that means, {other}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bone meal for everyone?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bone meal for me. You get my best wishes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The rabbits were at the carrots again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Build a fence, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I did. The little beasts waited until I left the gate open.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I've got Mending on offer, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Really? Since when?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Since this morning. And I plan to tell everyone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone broke my lectern and put it back again. Again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what changed?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now I'm selling books on Fire Protection. I feel... used.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I sell ender pearls. Don't ask how I got them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How did you get them?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I said don't ask.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My brewing stand is bubbling so cheerfully today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What are you brewing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A potion of patience. It isn't done yet. That's the whole joke.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Chainmail is underrated, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can see through the holes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's called ventilation.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My blast furnace smelts ore twice as fast as a normal furnace.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what do you do with the time you save?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I stand next to it and feel proud of myself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you know what a grindstone does to enchantments?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No idea. What?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It takes them away and gives you a little experience back. Just like life.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Have you seen what the armorer is charging today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Too much?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Far too much. I, of course, charge exactly the right amount.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A diamond pickaxe, {other}. Want to hold it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can I?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But it's nice that you asked.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gold tools are the fastest there are.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So they're the best?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They break after a handful of stones. Breaking fast still counts as fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I fished up a saddle today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Out of the river?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. I'm still wondering who rode in there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A pufferfish looked at me, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what did it want?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing. It just puffed up. I think I offended it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For arrows I need flint, sticks and feathers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where do you get the feathers?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: From the chickens. We don't talk about it, the chickens and I.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Today I shot an arrow straight through another one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On purpose?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm telling everyone it was on purpose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I dyed a sheep light blue, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why would you do that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I could find it in the meadow. Now I keep mistaking it for the sky.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Have you ever seen a pink sheep?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. Do they even exist?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Very rarely. If you ever see one, you get to make a wish.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My smoker's been running since early morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You can smell it all the way to the well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You're welcome.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rabbit stew today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What goes into that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rabbit, carrot, baked potato, mushroom and a bowl. And the nerve to take a carrot from the farmer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone wanted leather armor for their horse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you make it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They wanted purple. I only had brown. We settled on brown.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you know you can wash dye back out in a cauldron?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Handy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Vital. You should have seen that green.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I cut two hundred stone bricks today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With the stonecutter?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With passion. And with the stonecutter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Glazed terracotta in sixteen colors, {other}. Pick one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The grey one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Of all the colors. The grey one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I sold a map to a woodland mansion.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is that far?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Far enough that I'm not coming along. Say hi to the evokers for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On my maps the village always sits nicely in the middle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because that's how the world is laid out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because I live here. That's how maps work.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I worked today, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Really? On what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I looked at a block. Very thoroughly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why don't I have a workstation, anyway?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe none of them suit you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or I'm too good for all of them. Yes. That must be it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm still looking for a job, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ever tried a lectern?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Someone took it away again. Twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a free composter over there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then take it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm scared of the responsibility. And of pumpkins.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I've got saplings from places you'll never see.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One emerald. The places aren't included in the price.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My llamas don't like your village, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How can you tell?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They spit. All right, they spit everywhere. But here they mean it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's supposed to be a trap in the temple over there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What sort of trap?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A pressure plate with enough TNT underneath for three villages. I'm not going in, that's for sure.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you know what's painted on the walls of the old pyramid?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cacti?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three gods. A red dragon with two mouths, a blue giant and a golden dragon with wings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what did they mean?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say you had to make three sacrifices just to summon one of them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they can stay on the wall, thank you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My grandfather swore he once saw Obelisk the Tormentor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Out here in the desert?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: During a sandstorm. He said the giant just punched the ground and every cactus toppled over.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Our cacti topple over if you just put a block next to them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whenever the night sky glows red, my mother says Slifer the Sky Dragon is flying past.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And when it glows gold?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it's the Winged Dragon of Ra. Or the sun is coming up. Usually it's the sun.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: See the horses out there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. And not one of them will let me ride it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you know the sunflowers all face east?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even in the evening?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even in the evening. Even at night. They made up their minds once and they're sticking to it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The nitwit could learn a thing or two from them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I saw a bee flying back to its nest today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you help yourself to some honey?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Without a campfire underneath? I'm not out of my mind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The foxes stole all the sweet berries again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every single one?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One still had a berry in its mouth and stared right at me. The cheek of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I built a snow golem.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a pumpkin head?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Of course. Without a head it's just a pile of snow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So where is he now?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He was set on going to the desert. I couldn't stop him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a light on in the hut in the swamp again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is the witch back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or she never left and has just been brewing very quietly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On full moon nights there are more slimes bouncing around here than usual.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I'll stay indoors whenever the moon is full.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A parrot's been sitting on my shoulder for hours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How did you manage that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I didn't. It picked me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whatever you do, don't give it a cookie.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you see the armadillo? It rolled right up into a ball.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe it's shy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or it heard you talking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the badlands you find gold even way up high.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we'll be rich in no time!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Only if somebody takes gold. Everyone around here wants emeralds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Typical. Gold is always worthless exactly when you've got some.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The turtles are laying eggs on the beach again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then watch your step. They break more easily than you'd think.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The cow here is red and has mushrooms on its back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what comes out if you milk it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With a bowl you get mushroom stew. Don't ask me how that works.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Under the cherry trees, everything's pink.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Even the ground. The petals just land everywhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I brought a few home today. On my head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They suit you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Up here in the meadow it hums all day long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The bees have a lot on their plate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: More than we do. Maybe we should take a leaf out of their book.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tomorrow. Today we're just watching.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you know what lies beneath the waves out there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Squid and seagrass?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A sunken city. Atlantis. With towers of prismarine and lights that never go out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's just an ocean monument.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's what everyone says. But the guardians aren't down there protecting wet rocks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And who's diving down to check?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I don't have Water Breathing. I just tell the stories.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: At night the drowned climb out of the water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some even carry a trident. I'd love one. Preferably in my hand, not in my back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the dark forest it's already dim by noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why giant mushrooms grow there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And that's why zombies wander around there in daytime. The sun just can't get through.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Birch wood is so pale you can see every smudge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then build your house out of dark oak. You won't see anything at all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The flower forest has nearly every color you could imagine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The shepherd's been here three times today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And? Did they pick anything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. They stared at the flowers for ages, then at the sheep. Then back at the flowers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Uh-oh. That means colorful wool.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The frogs croak here all night long.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In exchange, they eat the little slimes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Useful, yes. Quiet, no.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say there's emerald ore in the windswept hills.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So our savings are just lying around inside a mountain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And not one of us owns a pickaxe. Typical village.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Up here a goat will ram you off the mountain before you can say hello.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did that happen to you?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Almost. I said hello in time.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And that helped?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But at least I fell politely.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The ice spikes here look like someone nailed the sky to the ground.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's hope it holds.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's powder snow in the grove. You just sink right in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not with leather boots.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I suppose I'll have to buy from the leatherworker. They'll be thrilled.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear that dripping?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the dripstone. Put a cauldron underneath and it slowly fills up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And if I stand underneath myself?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then sooner or later the tip lands on your head. Better not.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The glow berries light up the whole cave.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And you can eat them, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First they shine, then you eat them. Seems like a fair deal to me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shh. Not so loud.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I didn't say a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You breathed. And the sculk sensor over there clicked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then from now on I'll breathe very quietly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. And sneak while you're at it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: These trees are so tall I can't see their tops anymore.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They were standing here long before our village existed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A polar bear stared at me while I was standing on the ice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did it have a cub with it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. And I've rarely run that fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The panda over there sneezed again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did another slimeball come out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I didn't look too closely. Some things you'd rather not know.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There are squid in the river.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's why the librarian never runs out of ink.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On the stony shore every wave crashes loudly against the rocks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: At least nobody can sneak up on you here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The crabs could. Oh wait, those don't exist.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The piglins here trade anything for gold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For emeralds too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They don't want emeralds. They simply have no taste.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There are no hoglins in the warped forest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why's that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're scared of the warped fungi. Honestly, so am I.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You can barely move on soul sand.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the wailing in the wind doesn't help either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the basalt deltas it rains ash.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the magma cubes bounce right in front of you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I miss the rain. Never thought I'd say that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In the morning the whole village smells of fresh bread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's not bread. That's the butcher's smoker.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fresh pork chops, then. I'm not complaining.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sun's going down. Time to shut the doors.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the shutters. And the trapdoors. And ideally your eyes as well.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear that shrieking up there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Phantoms. Someone hasn't slept in days again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Must be the librarian. Reads all night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or you. You don't exactly look well rested either.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rain is good for the fields.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And bad for my hair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You don't have hair, {other}. You have a hat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In a thunderstorm I never stand next to the church.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How come?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lightning. If one of us gets struck, they turn into a witch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's just a rumor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you go stand there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In storms like this, a yellow bird is said to come out of the clouds. The old folks call it Zapdos.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A bird, in the middle of a storm?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It bathes in the lightning. That's why you only ever see it in weather like this.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's so dark down here I can't even see my own nose.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a nose like yours, that's quite an achievement.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thank you. I think.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear that flapping? That's a whole lot of bats.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let's hope they're not Zubat. Caves always have far too many of those.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How did we even end up here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone pushed us through a purple portal.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I hope they come back to fetch us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's no day or night out here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then how am I supposed to know when my shift ends?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bedtime already. Where's my bed?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wherever you left it yesterday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The nitwit's sleeping in it now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Welcome to village life.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm awake. My head isn't yet.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Give it time. Mine usually catches up around noon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not feeling well, {other}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stay close to the iron golem. He'll look after you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And who looks after me while he's handing out flowers?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mornin', {other}. Heard the smith yet today?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You always hear the smith.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hammerin' all day long. No fish'll bite with that racket.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He says your fish isn't fresh.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not fresh? Me fish is fresher than his whole anvil! I'll slap him round the ears with a cod, so I will.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did I ever tell ye I used to go to sea?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Several times.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I was a sea captain. I hold licenses A1, A3, A4 and A6!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And now you fish in the village pond.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Aye. But with style.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pulled out a golden-red carp today. Magikarp, the old folks call it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is it worth anything?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothin'. It just flops about.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then throw it back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not on yer life! Throw it back too often and one day it turns into a Gyarados. Heaven help us all then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Me gran always said there's a city under the sea with golden roofs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Atlantis?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Aye. And if ye keep real quiet at night, ye can hear its bells down there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the guardians from the ocean monument.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ye've not got a romantic bone in yer body, have ye?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The fisherman came by again, complaining about my noise.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what did you tell him?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That you can smell his fish all the way to my forge. We haven't spoken since.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The weaponsmith reckons the best defense is a good offense.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sounds reasonable enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sounds like someone who doesn't sell armor.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I read a book about a boy who lived under the stairs.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How sad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then an owl brought him a letter, and suddenly he was a wizard.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: All I get are phantoms. And they don't bring letters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm reading about two little folk who have to throw a ring into a fiery mountain.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why not any old lava? There's plenty about.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It has to be that one mountain. And getting there takes three thick books.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Couldn't they have just flown there on a big eagle?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Scholars are still arguing about that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I sold a map to a jungle temple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is that dangerous?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Arrow traps, tripwires, and supposedly at some point a giant stone ball comes rolling after you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who'd go there willingly?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A man with a hat and a whip. He said it all belongs in a museum.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An adventurer in a hat once told me: X never marks the spot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It does on your treasure maps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. That's why he found my maps boring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I left a blank spot on one of my maps because of something I saw there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did you see?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A small pink creature with a long tail. Scholars call it Mew. They say it carries the legacy of every creature in the world.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then why isn't it on the map?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Because it turned invisible the moment I picked up my pen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You know what would make life easier?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: More rain?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A little ball you could just pop an animal into. A cow, zap, straight into your pocket.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if it doesn't work?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you throw another one. And another.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My grandfather told me a huge sleeping beast once blocked the road to the next village.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And how did they wake it up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: With a flute. Snorlax, the beast was called. Ate half our harvest while it was at it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Emeralds are missing from my chest again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three. Exactly three. Same as last week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe you miscounted.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm a cartographer. I never miscount.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you hear? The cartographer's missing emeralds again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It wasn't me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I never said it was.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I just wanted that on record.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now you're a suspect.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I think the cat is stealing the cartographer's emeralds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cats bring you presents, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Just not to him. To someone else.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The emerald's looking weak today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Against what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Against wheat. Twenty wheat for one emerald, that's daylight robbery.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then hold on to your emeralds. Prices always bounce back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I've raised the price of bookshelves.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On what grounds?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Supply and demand. And an adventurer who bought every single one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There are 10 kinds of villagers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Only ten?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Those who understand binary, and those who don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Infinitely many villagers line up at the farmer's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Go on.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The first wants a loaf, the second half a loaf, the third a quarter, and so on.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what does the farmer do?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He puts down two loaves and says: you lot need to know your limits.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Parallel walls have so much in common.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is that a bad thing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's sad. They'll never meet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I read a fairy tale set in a galaxy far, far away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's a galaxy?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something like the End, only with far more stars. And no endermen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sounds cozy. What's it about?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A farm boy on a desert planet with two suns dreams of finally getting away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two suns? The zombies must burn twice as fast.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then he meets an old hermit who teaches him to move things with nothing but his mind.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I want that. I'd never have to haul wood again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And in the end it turns out the villain in the black armor is his father.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I did not see that coming.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yesterday a stranger walked into my house and said: My name is Geronimo Röder. I live here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And? Does he?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But he sounded so sure that for a moment I doubted it myself.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he at least offer rent?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you know Geronimo Röder? Best archer the forests have ever seen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've never seen him shoot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody has. For years he never found a single arrow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then sell him some.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He never comes by when I've got any.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A woodsman spent three hours explaining to me why foxes love stealing sweet berries.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Geronimo Röder? He knows more about every animal than the animal does.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There was a fellow in the next village called Stanley Balls. Ex-special forces, underwear model, and supposedly the strongest man for miles.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And was he?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He tried to lift an anvil to prove it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How did that go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The anvil won. Stanley says he let it win on purpose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a smith's son called Schmorf in the next village.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is he any good?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No idea. He always wears a bicycle helmet and talks to his broom.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And what does the broom say back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Only nice things, apparently. Which is more than I can say for my customers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yesterday someone climbed the church tower wall without a ladder.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who does a thing like that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Zacharias Bergmann. Didn't say a word, had a look around at the top and was gone again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a tale about four people who saved the world from the zombies with a serum.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a serum?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's what they called it. I'd have used a potion of weakness and a golden apple.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You always make saving the world sound so easy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An old count came to visit. He ate by the window and looked down on us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he say anything?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ah, I know those. They're the poor. They always stand outside my window when I eat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And his butler?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He just muttered: I hate my life. And then he was suddenly gone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Remember when the old count with the monocle was here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one whose monocle can sense magic?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's him. Ever since, the cartographer's been missing emeralds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So you're saying...

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm not saying anything. I've just been paying attention.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord Henry Gray told me three times today that he's very, very rich.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In one conversation?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In one sentence.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And did he buy anything?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. He said haggling was beneath him, then joked that fencing was his strong point. Nobody laughed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A French doctor, Francois Fuillaume De Tesseraque, wanted to sew pig legs onto our chicken.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whatever for?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He said: For science! I am ze specialist!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the chicken?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ran off faster than ever. On its own legs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A man with a golden mane, a leather jacket and three pairs of sunglasses came through the village today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One on his nose, two on his head. He introduced himself as Eduard Laser, let all the chickens out of the coop and shouted: For freedom!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did the chickens even want to be freed?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But he said: Freedom matters to me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the little one in the matching outfit?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lauchboy, his son. Afterwards he quietly caught the chickens again and secured the coop with redstone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Some fellow called Eduard Laser came to buy weapons from me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did he take?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing. Said he only fights with laser slaps and laser kicks. I have no idea what those are supposed to be.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Have you ever seen a baby zombie riding a chicken?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A chicken jockey? Those are real?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh yes. Word is, in some faraway world people cheered so loudly at the sight that popcorn went flying.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A trader told me that far to the south, the sun vanished in the middle of the day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some kind of spell?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, the moon slid in front of it. People stared up at the sky through dark glasses.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the zombies? Did they come out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He didn't say. I'd have gone to bed, just to be safe.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: In a faraway land, forty-eight teams supposedly fought over a single ball.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Forty-eight? Who's supposed to remember all those banners?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The pillagers' banner is more than enough for me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There was another poppy outside my door this morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the third this week, isn't it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The fourth. I've been counting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You've got a secret admirer!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or someone's hinting that I'm neglecting my flowerbed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you find a poppy at your door too?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. So did the smith. And the librarian.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it's not an admirer. It's someone who likes everybody.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who on earth likes everybody?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's exactly the question.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you hear the bell last night?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Three times. And not a pillager in sight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who rings a bell at night when there's no danger at all?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe someone who can't sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or someone who doesn't want us to sleep.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last night I sat down next to the bell and waited.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you see anyone?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Just a cat. It looked at me like it knew more than I did.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cats always know more than we do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every morning there's a new hole in my field.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An animal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An animal with a shovel?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Maybe someone's looking for treasure from one of the cartographer's maps.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then they could at least fill the holes back in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A plumber in a red cap came by and jumped head-first into every block he could find.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What's the point of that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He said sometimes coins fall out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And did anything fall out?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But afterwards he had a bump the size of a mushroom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The plumber was asking about a princess.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does one live here?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. I told him his princess is in another castle.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We don't even have a castle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. He didn't seem surprised, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The turtles on the beach are so peaceful.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not all of them. There are tales of a huge turtle king with spikes on his shell who kidnaps princesses.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And ours?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The most they'd kidnap is seagrass.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yesterday a boy in green clothes and a pointy cap came into the village.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did he want?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No idea. He didn't say a single word.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he do anything at all?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. He went into every house and smashed all the pots.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And nobody stopped him?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How? He never answered.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I saw someone hitting a chicken over and over again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did he stop eventually?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. When suddenly every chicken in the village went for him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Our chickens? But they're so peaceful.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Some people could push even a chicken too far.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: An adventurer wanted an empty bottle to catch a fairy in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A fairy? What on earth for?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If he collapses, she's meant to wake him back up. I sold him a healing potion instead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Know what a plumber once told me about red mushrooms?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That you can't eat them raw?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That they make you twice as big. I tried, but I can't even get the thing down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a tale about a sword in a stone that only a true hero can pull out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And who forged it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody knows. But a sword nobody can pull out is bad for business.
